content.title: Lists, Keys, and Identity
content.context:
```jsx
const items = [
  { id: "a", name: "Mug" },
  { id: "b", name: "Notebook" }
];
```

You can turn them into UI:

```jsx
items.map(item => (
  <ProductRow key={item.id} name={item.name} />
))
```

The `key` is not a decoration.

It gives React a stable identity for a repeated item within that list.
goals: Understand why repeated React children need stable keys and how keys help React match elements across renders.

options.text: The displayed price, even if prices can repeat

feedback.correct: A stable identifier should stay attached to the same logical item across renders.
feedback.incorrect: A stable identifier should stay attached to the same logical item across renders.

content.title: Why identity matters
content.text:
Imagine a list where each row contains its own input value.

Then the list gets reordered.

If React can reliably identify each row, it can preserve the correct relationship between the row and its state.

If identity is unstable, the UI can appear to “move” state to the wrong item.

content.question:
This is often tempting:

```jsx
items.map((item, index) => (
  <ProductRow key={index} {...item} />
))
```

Is the index always wrong?

options.text: No. It can be acceptable when the list is truly static and items never reorder, insert, or delete in a way that changes their positions.

feedback.correct: The engineering concern is whether the key represents stable identity. Index keys become risky when position and identity can diverge.
feedback.incorrect: The engineering concern is whether the key represents stable identity. Index keys become risky when position and identity can diverge.

content.question: A queue can reorder as new items arrive. Which key is safer?

feedback.correct: Position can change; identity should not.
feedback.incorrect: Position can change; identity should not.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A key answers: “Which logical item is this across renders?”
**Senior habit:** When list behavior becomes weird, inspect identity before changing rendering logic.
nextSteps: Explain why a stable item ID is usually a better key than an array index for a changing list.
